utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much. Today is Wednesday, 21st of January, 2009. I'd like to say good morning to all. The representatives of the Defence, the Office of the Prosecution, and all of the people who work in the courtroom day after day with great devotion. I believe Mr. Scott has a question. Mr. Scott, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, Mr. President, each of Your Honours. Judge Prandler, I apologise for the location of the pole in the courtroom. Please forgive me. To counsel and all those in and around the courtroom thank you very much. Your Honour, I need to raise -- I need to take a bit of the Chamber's time this morning I'm afraid to raise with the Chamber an issue that needs -- because of the time it needs to be dealt with further, we submit, Your Honour, and that has to do with the request -- the Prosecution's pending request for a fully adequate summary for Mr. Bozic, who comes next week. Excuse me, Your Honour. I apologise. Your Honour, let me just say that this is not an issue that's new to the Chamber. The matter has been raised going all the way back, in fact, to some of the Pre-Defence Conferences in April last year in which the Chamber made its views quite clear as to what was required for these summaries. And then there are a number of instances throughout the Prlic case where the Prosecution raise its concerns, and on a number of occasions, not every occasion, but on a number of occasions the Chamber saw fit to order additional summaries to be provided. Let me just stop and say briefly about the law, Your Honour. There may be a number of areas of Tribunal law that for one reason or another may remain not entirely clear. This is not one of them. The Tribunal law on this topic has been well established, and it is -- I think I can accurately summarise it as this: Rule 65 ter requires an advance meaningful summary of what the evidence of the witness will actually be. That is not simply a biographical background, he held these positions through the years. It is not simply a list of topics. It is meant to be a summary that both the Trial Chamber, the Judges, and the Prosecution, and for that matter, the other parties, I should add, not just the Prosecution but including the co-accused, can have a meaningful -- can be on meaningful notice in order to meaningfully prepare to meet the evidence of that witness. It's very, very clear. Background and topics are not sufficient. And I submit to the Chamber that when reading these summaries, one of the ways -- frankly one of the buzzwords, if you will, or key words that gives away the nature of the summary provided is when it repeatedly says: "The witness will testify about." "The witness will testify about." "The witness will testify about." What the summary -- what the law requires is not what they will talk about the topic, in other words, the subject matter, but what they will say. Topic A, the witness will say that; topic B, the witness will say that. Not topics. The law is absolutely clear on that from both other Trial Chambers and from the Appeals Chamber, and this Chamber has had that law before on a number of times between now and last spring, and I'm sure perhaps before. Now, with that background in mind, Your Honour, with that background in mind, Your Honour, let me just review a bit of procedural history so the Chamber knows -- understands hopefully a bit more where the Prosecution is coming from in this particular instance. First of all, Your Honour, I start from my last comment. The law is clear and if there is any question of the Defence being on notice as to what is required of them, the law is clear; and it's been repeatedly briefed and addressed in this courtroom on a number of occasions. Nothing new. Number two, the obligation to provide fully adequate summaries was required and in complete force when the Defence filings were made on the 31st of March, 2008. We're coming up not quite there but we're coming up on that being a year ago. On the 31st of March, 2008, each of the Defence teams were required to meet the obligations up Rule 65 ter. This is not an obligation that sprung into existence last week, a few days ago, or two months ago. The obligation has been on the books. The Tribunal law has been clear for years and since the first obligation on the 31st of March, 2008, when the filings were made. Further than that, Your Honour, we have -- this Chamber again as I mentioned a moment ago, including Judge Antonetti, Your Honour, on the 21st of April, 2008, specifically said in reviewing the Defence filings on the 31st of March, 2008, that a number of the summaries were deficient and I can change the Chamber to those citations if necessary, but I can tell the Court, Judge Antonetti, you were very clear; and, in fact, you specifically said that a number of the Praljak summaries in particular were deficient. Further, trying to raise these issues in an ongoing way, the Prosecution anticipating the beginning of the Stojic Defence case, corresponded with counsel on several occasions, first on the 1st of October, 2008, again on 23 October, 2008, asking again and reminding them of the need to provide fully adequate summaries as required by Rule 65 ter. On the 5th of January of this year, we sent another -- yet another letter, at least the third letter, to the Stojic counsel again raising the issue and specifically as to the witnesses, Bozic and Buljan who are coming up in the near future. We afforded at that time, Your Honour, if -- well, let me put it this way. We reminded the Defence of the law's requirements and invited them to please provide an additional fully adequate summary not later than the 12th of January. Why the 12th of January? Because we need the time to prepare, number one. Number two, to provide the opportunity to bring the matter before the Chamber if the parties could not resolve it. So we were trying to find a creative situation which could be resolved without bringing it before the Chamber. Unfortunately, we did not receive any additional summary by the 12th of January, and as we indicated we would because of the pressure of the timing of the trial, the next day we file our motion requesting the fully adequate summary as required by Rule 65. That's a brief history of that aspect of the -- or -- of the procedure concerning this motion, Your Honour. We did receive, we did receive, I want to be clear, in the last few days a filing by the Defence, by the Stojic Defence, and a -- what is called an additional summary. With great respect, Your Honour, I have to say that while we appreciate in some sense the effort, it continues in the same deficiencies. It's again a list of topics. In fact, what they've done is add topics. They've expanded the number of topics that the witness will talk about but have not said anything about what his evidence will actually be. So, Your Honour, we feel that this matter's been fully -- fully ventilated. This is a matter that's not new to any of the parties in this case. The Prosecution has raised the issue a number of times as has the Chamber in general, as has the Chamber; and so we're back, Your Honour, to once more being on the Wednesday before the appearance of a witness without an adequate summary, and I would ask the Chamber before I give the floor over or answer any questions Your Honours might have. It is not adequate, and it is not what Rule 65 ter contemplates or requires that what happens at the end of the day is that on the eve of the witness's appearance, on the eve of the witness's appearance, the Prosecution and the Judges get an additional late summary which in its content may or may not be helpful. The Prosecution should have had these fully adequate summaries not later than 31st of March. Of course we understand the difficulties and the burdens involved in litigation. We know that, and that's why we haven't pressed harder up until now, but that's March 31st we're now in January 2009. We've raised the issue through last fall. We raised the issue again in early January of this year. So, Your Honour, that brings us to the point that since the witness is scheduled and we were also hoping to take notice of the timing - excuse me - to avoid unnecessary travel by the witness if possible, and our position, Your Honour, and what the Prosecution requests at this point, and I think there's just simply no other way than to finally get the attention that these things have to be done, we ask that the witness Bozic be postponed and not rescheduled unless and until fully adequate summary is provided. It's only when I think, Your Honour, with great respect when this message is clear and enforced that we can all then look forward hopefully to fully adequate summaries in the future. The Prosecution wants to raise this issue now at the very given, if you will, of the Stojic case, so we can hopefully get off on the right foot. So we raise it now, and I will have to say, Your Honour, if need be, we will continue to raise it as the Chamber's seen in the past. The Prosecution submits that we've been reasonable in this position. We've tried to address it without bringing it before the Chamber, but now we are where we are. I thank you for the Chamber's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Nozica, I will be giving you the floor in a moment. Indeed we are aware of this motion dated the 13th of January. When we met on the 19th, we thought that this had been solved between the Defence and the Office of the Prosecutor, and therefore we did not think we had to mention it again because we thought it had been solved; and I hear now that as of Monday the 19th of January you sent a supplementary document but apparently this summary is not satisfactory for the OTP. The OTP has now formally requested that we postpone the appearance of that witness and you understand I'm sure the risk involved. What do you have to say here?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good morning. Good morning to everybody in the courtroom. I would like to briefly say something. This topic has taken the most time in the court in the procedural sense. I would like to say that we submitted our 65 ter list. The Prosecutor today twice mentioned the date of March 2008. The OTP had no objection to our list of summaries. So they didn't have objections. We submitted, as Mr. Scott correctly said, a list of topics the witness will be testifying about. We would like to remind the Chamber that we also submitted the documents so that it may be clear which documents would be shown to the witness. Talking about Witness Bozic, I would like to remind the Chamber that the witness gave a statement to the OTP as a -- as a suspect. Most of these topics will be the subject of interrogation here in the courtroom. I understand the OTP to say, "Give us the statement." We are not obliged to submit the statement. We are obliged to give information about what the witness will be speaking and what the witness will specifically say about any topic is in fact a statement. As this issue will obviously be reappearing during the defence of Mr. Stojic, I ask that the Chamber to give me instructions. Apart from the summaries the Defence has submit and apart from the amendments we will submit for every witness if the witness should, in testifying, go beyond the topics mentioned in the summary, Mr. Bozic will come on Friday so that on Saturday at the latest, we will give additional details when this witness comes to be proofed, but what -- what was said about Mr. -- Witness Bozic, I repeat that Mr. Bozic was heard as a suspect is really inappropriate. So we will provide additional information as instructed by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Nozica, the Chamber will discuss this, and we will re-examine the 65 ter documents. We will look at the January 19th document, and we will inform you of our position. Either we decide that the January 19th document is satisfactory or we decide it isn't, but since I do not have it before me I cannot make that decision just now. But you have just said that you want the Chamber to give instructions as to how to proceed. Well, I cannot make a decision on behalf of the Chamber at this point, but the Chamber has been very clear thus far in the various decisions that we have handed down. We have requested that the parties provide a maximum amount of information, and I believe in fact in my opinion that it's in your very own interest to prepare long detailed summaries in such a way that you inform the Prosecution of the items, the points, the subjects you are going to be discussing with the witness in order to deal with certain facts in order to enable the Prosecution to prepare its cross-examination, and in that way the Judges are inform of your strategy and will better understand exactly what you are endeavouring to prove. I must say that sometimes when a witness comes to testify, on the basis of the resume, I really don't understand what you're trying to prove. If you were to provide fuller, more detailed resumes where you explain point by point exactly what you are trying to prove it would be far easier for us to understand. Now, I can understand from a strategic point of view that you don't want to show all your cards, but at this stage in the presentation of the evidence on the part of the Defence you do have to show your cards. You can't keep them in hiding, so to speak, till the very end. When you're calling a witness, when it's your own witness, you have to show your hand, and in presenting a full resume you would be doing just that. You can understand that the Prosecutor prepares his cases in advance as well. When you have 15 binders, he's going to have 20, and therefore that's the case because he has to counter what you're -- what you're stating. And we can understand, therefore, that he has a real need to have a detailed resume. This is an issue that we've discussed in the past. We have now heard an oral request on the part of the Prosecutor, accompanied with a written submission that we have just received this very moment, and we will decide on the basis of the January 19th resume, and we will inform you later in the day. That's what I can say at this point. If the Chamber decides to postpone the witness, we will tell you immediately to avoid that the witness have to travel for no purpose. So we will give you the response later. I will ask the legal counsel of the Chamber to inform you very rapidly regarding the January 19th statement. Can we call the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is exactly why I -- I wanted to hear the position of the Chamber because it is obvious that these demands will be repeated, and we know before the first -- or the following witness the position of the OTP, and we don't want things like this to be repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that Mr. Karnavas is ready and has been ready for several moments. His file is open. Mr. Karnavas, I believe each of you has 30 minutes for your examination. There are three of you who are speaking. That makes an hour and a half for the three. So maybe you've shared out the time differently. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe you're correct, Mr. President. Good morning, Mr. President; good morning, Your Honours. I hope to be 30 minutes or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Marijan. Sorry for keeping you waiting. We had a procedural matter to settle, and therefore you have just come into the courtroom, and I'm going to call upon Mr. Karnavas, who is going to proceed with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Again good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And good morning, Mr. Marijan.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we have your report here. We heard your testimony, and I want to pick up where we left off yesterday where you indicated to counsel for Mr. Stojic that you stand by your report having made one correction, and I thought that perhaps we could clarify a few matters. If you could look at your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Usher, do we have -- Mr. Usher, does the gentleman have all the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to be referring to your report somewhat, only a few topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We'll begin by looking at paragraph number 13, Your Honours. If you could get your report out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, could you be a bit closer to your microphone. It's a little difficult for the interpreters to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I don't want to be shouting, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have your report, sir? At paragraph 13, in here you state at the beginning of the paragraph that the heads of departments -- the head of the Department of Defence was accountable for his work to the HVO of the HZ HB, and further down in the same paragraph you indicate that -- the HVO adopted reports and proposals of the Department of Defence and gave instructions and guide-lines to the Department of Defence, and I take it you stand by that -- that part of your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just by way of an example just so we can show everyone, if we were to look at -- you have my binder there. We're going to look at P 03796. It should be towards -- towards the back. Okay. P 03796. These are minutes of a meeting dated 29 July 1993. If we look at the very first page in English at least where we have the agenda, under number 14 it says "Other matters." And if we go to the end of the report, almost at the very end, here we have, for instance -- we see that: "It is recommended that in the future the Department of Defence should issue timely reports about the situation at the front line to the public and to the members of leading bodies of the HVO HZ HB." Do you have that, sir? 3796. It's at the very last page. This is just as an example of where, for instance, instructions or guide-lines in this instance they're recommending to the Department of Defence to provide timely reports about the front line. This would be one example where you state, for instance, that the Department of Defence is being given instructions by the HVO HZ HB; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the reason I want to point that out is because if we go now to your report on paragraph 12, here you state: "The deputy head and assistant head of the Department of Defence were appointed by the president of the HVO, Jadranko Prlic." And you mention Slobodan Bozic. Then again if we were to turn to paragraph 19 of your report, we see again where you make reference that Mr. Bozic was appointed by Jadranko Prlic, the president of the HVO. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. These are not trick questions. We're very easy to answer. Now, is it your position, sir, and I want to be -- I guess I want to lock you into a position; is it your position that it was Dr. Prlic who actually made these appointments or that these appointments were made by the HVO HZ HB as a collective body? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, Your Honours, I would like to see those appointments, but I believe that Mr. Prlic signed all these appointments. Of course he signed on behalf of the HVO but also in his own name. I actually don't quite understand what you want to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me help you out here. P 01137, P 01137.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look at, Your Honours, item number 7 on the first page which says "Personal matters" -- "Personnel matters," I'm sorry, and if we go to -- it would be page number 5, Your Honours, in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if you go to -- find that document, sir, and go to addendum number 7. It would be page 3 for you, sir. And is says here --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Great. Great. Super. "At the proposal of the head of the Defence Department the HVO HZ HB Slobodan Bozic is appointed deputy head of the Defence department of the HVO HZ HB." Do you see that sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it a member of the HVO HZ HB was none other than Mr. Stojic. In other words, he was not only proposing, but one can also assume that he would have voted had he been there, or someone would have voted in his stead if somebody was there on behalf of the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no doubt that Mr. Stojic was a member of the HVO because he was head of department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And we see that it's the HVO, do we not, that actually makes the decision base on the proposal of Mr. Stojic; right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can draw that conclusion from this item.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "you," are you saying me personally, or should we use the word "we," that we can draw that conclusion? Which of the two? Because I've already drawn that conclusion, but I want you to draw it as well.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusion as I said in this specific case is the follows: That the head of the Defence, Mr. Bozic was appoint as deputy head, and that the HVO agreed to that, gave its agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Then one more just to make sure that we finish with this topic, at least with Mr. Bozic. If we look at P 006 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, I am a bit surprised. Perhaps there was a problem in translation. You said that the HVO approved the decision. The document, rather, suggests that the HVO takes the decision, not someone else took actually the decision and made the appointment, and the HVO just sort of rubber stamped or approved, nihil obstat, but they took the decision. It's their decision. That's how I read the document. Do you have a different opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, well, I have the impression that that's what I said too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It may be a problem of translation. It would not be the first one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can go to now P 00615. And there are several decisions that we see in there. You will find if you -- if you page through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it would be on page 19, Your Honours in the English version, one that refers to Mr. Slobodan Bozic, law graduate from Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could find it. Towards the middle of the document -- or towards the end of it, I should say. Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas -- Mr. Karnavas, I know something similar to what you've been saying, but I can't find it. You said 615, did you? Was that the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: P 00615. Page number 19 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only have the English version but I've found it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me just read out part of the English version. It says here: "Pursuant to Article 18 of the statutory decision," and it goes on and on. It then goes on. It refers to Article 31, paragraph 2 of the degree on the organisation and competence of the department and commissions of the HVO HZ HB as proposed by the head of the HVO HZ HB Defence Department, the HVO HZ HB at the session held 15 January 1993, and we have a decision. Article 1 we see Slobodan Bozic's name. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, going back to your report, your report does not state that it's the HVO HZ HB that actually takes the decision as a collective body, but what you have, sir, is that it is Jadranko Prlic who actually makes the appointment. Now, my question to you is: Is your report accurate when we look at these documents, or would you like an opportunity to correct your report here and now?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I stand by my findings, and that's why I asked you the question whether there's any things you wish to clarify. Is what you're saying this: Do you mean to say that Mr. Prlic was on the same level with all the members of the HVO? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me put it to you this way, sir --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I understand it correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me put it to you this way, sir: We heard from Mr. Buntic. We heard from Mr. Petkovic. We heard from Martin Raguz. We also heard from Mr. Tomic, and with Mr. Tomic in particular it was none other than Ms. Senka Nozica that cross-examined to establish that decisions are taken by the collective body. And now I put to you, sir, are these not the decisions of the collective body and not, as you suggest in your report, the decisions of Dr. Jadranko Prlic?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the one hand these are collective decisions of the HVO as the executive body, but in its name that executive body has a person at its head, and whenever we refer to the HVO here, and I think Judge Trechsel said on one occasion, in inverted commas, he put this under quotation marks when he said "government," but put it in quotation marks, as I say, because it's called the way it was called, anyway, from the documents we can see that the body made the decisions collectively, but the body did have a person at the head who signed on behalf of that collective body. And I look at -- I looked at the statutory Decision on the Temporary Organisation of the Executive Authority. I think that's what the title was. That's what it was called, of the 3rd of July, 1992, and I refer to it in one place, I believe, and that's how I understood it, that all the members of the HVO were accountable for their work to Mr. Prlic, were responsible to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let's look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours. I wonder if I might make a small practical observation to tie Mr. Karnavas's examination to the report. The document Mr. Karnavas has been referring to which is P 00615 appears to be for practical purposes the same as the one referred to in footnote 48 of the witness's report which is P 01136; and I think if one appreciates that they are the same item it's going to be much easier to tie Mr. Karnavas's cross-examination together with the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at paragraph 25 of your report, here you -- you say: "The HVO president appointed chiefs of Defence administration at the recommendation of the head of the Department of Defence."

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then you go on to say: "The president of the HVO established," established, "the internal organisation." And of course we can see your footnote number 68, document 988? Now, when you say it is Dr. Jadranko Prlic here that appointed, are you not suggesting that it was his appointment and not the appointment of the collective body? Are you not suggesting that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes or no. It's a yes or no, sir. Are you suggesting that or not? You're an educated man. You know how to read. Are you making that suggestion that he made the appointment? Yes, no, I don't know, which of the three?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now let's look at number 31, paragraph 31.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise to my colleague Mr. Karnavas. However, I can't catch up. I can't follow. Now, Mr. Karnavas referred to paragraph 25 of the report. Would he allow the witness time to find that paragraph and the circumstances surrounding it, because it says the Defence ministry -- internal organisation of the Defence administrations signed by the president of the HVO, Jadranko Prlic in 1993 I see nothing to be challenged there but if the witness isn't given time to read the whole text then he can't answer. So there's no need to go that fast. So could he please allow time for the witness to read through the whole paragraph and see the circumstances to which he refers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's look at paragraph number 31. Here you say: "On October 1992, the president of the HVO, J. Prlic, appointed Ivica Lucic to the position of assistant head of Defence department for security." Same question. You have the paragraph in front of you, do you not I sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the paragraph and the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, are you not suggesting here, sir that it is Dr. Jadranko Prlic who appoints Ivica Lucic, that it's his appointment? Isn't that what you're trying to suggest here?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision by Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now let's look at P 00578. P 00578.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, you will find it on -- we're looking at item 6, paragraph -- on page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, it says here, and I'll read, and if I read anything wrong you correct me: "Head of the Defence department Mr. Bruno Stojic proposed adopting a decision to appoint Mr. Ivica Lucic lawyer from Ljubuski, assistant head of the Defence Department for security. "The draft decision to appoint Mr. I. Lucic was unanimously adopted." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read the item, and I do see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is it Mr. Prlic who unanimously adopts it by himself or is it the collective body of the HVO HZ HB that takes a vote and makes a decision, a collective decision, a decision which belongs to the HVO HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I can see that there was a vote on this decision and they all voted in favour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And whose decision is it, sir? Because earlier you told us that the appointment -- the appointment was Dr. Prlic's. So whose appointment was it, the HVO's or Dr. Prlic's? Which of the two, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appointment -- Mr. Karnavas, the appointment was carried out by the president of the HVO, Dr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, don't be simple with me. You have a Ph.D. For a living you read documents. My question is very simple. Whose -- who made the decision for the appointment, Mr. Prlic or the HVO HZ HB? Which of the two? Come clean, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I really do have a Ph.D., yes, and I know what an executive body means; and I know that an executive body is the only collective body that I know of in the region of the former Yugoslavia that was made up of equal members. There was the Presidency of the SFRY, but this did not function in that way. Therefore, the members, all the members of the HVO as an executive body was not a conglomerate or a collection or a body in which everybody was equal, had an equal footing. With the exception of one person all the others were equal, but as far as I understand it, that body had its head who was not equal to all the other members but above them, and he was the sole individual, as far as I understand it, who could have sign this decision, and it was Mr. Prlic, if I understood correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall testifying before the Tuta-Stela case and informing the Trial Chamber at the time that you were not a lawyer? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's common knowledge from my CV that I'm not a lawyer. So there's nothing to add there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And were questions put to you about the -- about the government authorities, at which point in Tuta-Stela you indicated that you are an historian and could give an opinion as an historian and not a lawyer? Do you recall saying that? You were being questioned, I believe, by Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was -- it was seven years, ago, was it? I don't remember that. Most probably that's the case if you found it in the transcript. However, I didn't write this as a lawyer. I wrote it as an historian. So I'm not interpreting the law here --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that was not my intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's look at P 00615, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just a clarification. You're not a lawyer. We all know that. Still, in your report as it stands, it can appear that Mr. Prlic appointed a person X to such and such position. One can conclude from this that Mr. Prlic has the power to make appointments. With this document on the screen, we find out that in the actuality, Mr. Ivica Lucic was appointed after unanimous deliberation and decision. So the procedure would be as follows: Mr. Stojic makes proposals, submits proposals, and everyone agrees to the appointment, after which Mr. Prlic signs the document. And in listening to both of you, I was trying to place myself in the shoes of a Judge signing a decision. As a Presiding Judge, when I sign a decision, I sign a decision on which it was deliberated, sometimes after a vote, and I put my signature. And sometimes I even sign a decision when I disagree with the decision. So I sign. I have a power. I have to sign, must sign, even though I have not made the decision. In the light of this, of the procedure, three stages: One, proposal of draft decision; second, deliberation; and third, somebody who's got the competence to sign, would that change what you stated in your report or does it remain the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understood it -- well, it's clear to me that the HVO made decisions. I assume had most of the body been against the decision it would not have been passed. I understand that, but -- well ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe it's a non-answer answer, Your Honour. And I am pressing the witness because now, at this point, I'm calling him incompetent or a liar, either two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't go that far. Witness, there was the deliberation that decided to it appoint Mr. Lucic, but let's imagine Mr. Prlic disagreed, but all the others agreed with the draft decision. Lucic was appointed, and Mr. Prlic had to sign even though he may have disagreed. In such a case, in the decision, there would be a note that the proposal was carried with majority, et cetera. But does that mean, according to you, Mr. Prlic, it is -- the appointment was Mr. Prlic's responsibility? This is the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I think that Mr. Prlic wouldn't bear the responsibility for that appointment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you -- you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So whose appointment is it? Is it the HVO in that instance or Dr. Prlic, which of the two and are you suggesting that when he votes for it, it's his appointment and when he votes against it it's not his appointment? Is that what you're suggesting, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood it correctly -- well, they were always unanimous decisions as far as I understood it, but, yes, the HVO did make collective decisions. I can see that from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, my question is -- is rather precise picking up on what the president asked you. Based on your answer, so if Prlic votes against an appointment, then it's not his appointment but it would be the HVO's appointment in your opinion. Is that what you're trying to tell us, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If he votes for the decision, if he votes for the appointment then it's his appointment, not the HVO's.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, well, it's difficult for me -- becoming difficult for me to follow, but what I can tell you is this: The HVO did make collective decisions, that's true, whether Mr. Prlic agreed or not. If he was out-voted, he would sign. Is that what you want to hear?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, it's not what I want to hear. I want to know what you are thinking. With Mr. Lucic you claim, you claim that this is his appointment, his decision. That's what you're claiming. Had Mr. Prlic voted against Mr. Lucic's appointment, would that be the HVO's appointment and not Mr. Prlic's, in your point of view? It's a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the decision would --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead. Continue. You don't need to look at the transcript. You can just answer the question.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So -- but now if Mr. Prlic had voted for Lucic to be appointed, then it would be Prlic's appointment, not the HVO's then?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit I am not following.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's why -- that's why I'm trying to clarify, sir, because on Article 31 -- paragraph 31 you make the insinuation that Lucic was appointed by Prlic. Now, do you make that decision to put that in because you see it was a unanimous vote and, therefore, you attribute the decision to Prlic and not to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's like this, Mr. Karnavas: Item 80, the appointment of Mr. Prlic, well, it was published in the Narodni List of the HZ HB, which makes it a public document, and from that public document it emerges, it follows -- or, rather, at least that part of the public documents that the appointment of the president of the HVO -- of course these minutes are not a public document and here we see the technology of it, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, we can look at P 00615, go back to that document. And we see in that document on page 10, Your Honours, a decision on Mr. Lucic, and I apologise for having to spend so much time on a rather simple issue, but here on page 10 in the English version, and if you can't find it I'll give you the B/C/S version, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you can come and we can assist this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here again --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, all right, I found the document. I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, again you see pursuant to Article 18 of the statutory decision there was a session held on 14th October 1992. We see that a decision is taken. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. To appoint a security assistant to the president of the HVO HZ HB, and we see it's Mr. Lucic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so we see that this decision is as a result of a session that was held on the 14th of October; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look at the earlier document we saw that at that particular session all the members that were present of the HVO HZ HB voted for and made the decision to appoint Mr. Lucic; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so from that, does it not follow, sir, that that decision and that appointment was of or by the HVO HZ HB and not, as you stated on paragraph 31, that it was Dr. Jadranko Prlic's appointment?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- Your Honours, I have to intervene. Mr. Marijan, on several occasions, has been repeating that the appointment was conducted by Mr. Jadranko Prlic, was carried out by him, and that's a logical term, because an appointment is made by one person and the selection can be made by a whole body, or the decision to select may be made by a body; and Mr. Marijan has been saying several times, has been referring to appointment, and there's no -- that's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it's such a decision which is proposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will interrupt because [Overlapping speakers] ... dishonest.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to protect -- no, no, I'm being quite frank, and I have to protect my witness because several times now, he's been repeating the term "appointment." Whether it's a problem with the English interpretation, I really don't know, so I wish to be of assistance because an appointment is signed in this case by Jadranko Prlic; and now I'm confused because he doesn't know what's being asked at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honour, let me be very clear. My colleague and I having worked in the region know that what we have just heard from Nozica is false. This is not an appointment by Prlic, and it's nonsense what we just heard. That objection is utter nonsense. It's gobbledegook. The gentleman is very clear and the insinuation is very clear that he wishes to make it the appointment by -- but by doing so we can show there's some kind of chain of command. That's the essence of all of this. And there's no issue with the translation. And unlike Ms. Nozica, Ms. Tomanovic knows English very, very well and can track both languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, first of all -- Mr. Karnavas, you have used up your 30 minutes. Witness, this is an issue of appointment. It needs to be looked at from a legal point of view because behind this appointment there is the power, the competence to make appointments who exercises the actual power or competence to a point and this is the underlying issue. Is it Mr. Prlic who decides thoroughly to appoint Mr. X to such and such position because he has this sovereign discretionary competence or power, or will Mr. Prlic appoint the witness but he has a limited competence, that is -- that is a prior procedure and which is not involved that is proposal by Mr. Stojic, then deliberation, then vote, if necessary, and a signature. So this is how things stand. Of course this can give rise to submissions by the counsels because they have their own point of views, but we need to be above this as Judges, but I'm putting the problem to you as it is presented to us. But reading your paragraph 31, according to you, it was Mr. Prlic's competence to make appointments, but maybe this is not what you meant. Maybe you meant something else. So what did you actually mean? Do you understand the difference between having the power or having limited competence? Are these concepts familiar to you, or do you not understand them? If that's the case, then we might as well call a halt to the discussion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if this calls --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the term "limited competence" or "qualified competence." We have very different legal concepts here, and perhaps translation can lead to misunderstandings, but since your legal system is very similar to mine, I think that when I say something you should perhaps understand it perhaps more easily than if I belonged to a different legal system.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If necessary, well, I'm looking at this text in front of me, and if necessary I may clarify this one sentence, and I may say that Mr. Jadranko Prlic, on behalf of the HVO, appointed Mr. Lucic to the position of the assistant head. But this is what I meant even before I said this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, I think we need to put an end to this discussion. This is a complex legal issue. The witness maintains his statement and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I need about 15 more minutes. I have a couple of more topics to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the record, on page 27, line 16, it's gone now, but maybe you have the possibility to look back, quotes you as mentioning or addressing Mr. Tomljanovich. It says Tomanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Tomanovic. It is Tomanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You wanted to say Tomanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Ms. Tomanovic, this is my co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I know, I know. Okay. It was surprising because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Not Mr. Tomljanovich, Ms. Tomanovic, my co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You just said you need another 15 minutes. Does that mean that one of your colleagues will be giving you 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of -- in light of the abstinence of this particular witness, I'm going to need for time. And yesterday the Trial Chamber was rather generous having, you know, given the -- the Stojic Defence additional time. So I do need to cover a couple of points because I do believe that it will assist the Trial Chamber in clarifying certain matters, and if not, I will -- I will at least want three minutes to make my offer of proof of the record of the topics that I would be going into in the event I'm not given the time. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you look at paragraph 95 of your report, yesterday you made reference to a document which is P 00646. It's referenced in footnote 217 of your report where you claim, you know, if we look at the bottom part of page 44, Your Honours, you say: "The HVO Main Staff was responsible to the work to the president of the HZ HB as the supreme commander of the armed forces of the HZ HB and the Security Sector, in addition to the president of the HZ HB also to the president of the HVO." And you quote that document. And I noticed yesterday you and counsel for Stojic were referring to the document as a work plan. That document, sir, is it not -- does it not say "Proposal"? Document P 00646. Is that not a proposal, sir, and not something that has been adopted?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. Karnavas. This was a proposal, but I believe I explained yesterday why I wrote what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, can you point anywhere, sir, because I've looked high, low, wide, and repeatedly, to find where at any of the sessions this proposal was adopted? Can you please point where, sir? In which session, at what time, this proposal was actually adopted?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any session at which this proposal would have been adopted, but I'm not sure that I saw all the documents from all the sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And some minutes -- minutes from some of the sessions that I did see were completely illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at document P 04211. And I believe you make reference to this in paragraph 38 of your report. And let's see because now we're into who's responsible for SIS. And when you're looking for the document, did you by any chance meet with Mr. Lucic? Did you make an attempt to meet with him, he's also an historian, as I understand, to discuss under who -- under who he was reporting to?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean whether we meet concerning this particular topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need to meet up --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- he reported to the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. To -- you mean Mr. Stojic; right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So there's no doubt that SIS was under Mr. Stojic, reported to Mr. Stojic, and Mr. Stojic was responsible for all their work; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no doubt about that, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course if we look at Article 42, I won't go through all of the articles, but 42 might be of an interest so we can actually see who's -- who's on top of him. Article 42, it talks about taping: "In order to prevent illegal activity by a individual, group, organisation, and foreign institutions, the service has resources to covert taping in order to uncover, monitor, and document this activity." If we go further down, we see that permission has to be obtained by the head, that is Mr. Stojic; correct? Not by the HVO, not by the president of the HVO HZ HB, but by Mr. Stojic himself; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look at Article 43 [Realtime transcript read in error, "17"] we see the same thing. We see secret taping of telephones and other means of communications. We see the same thing.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approved by the president, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Leave a pause between question and answer you're overlapping with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My apologies. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It says shall be approved by the head, not the president, by the head. That means Mr. Stojic; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Beg your pardon? You're going to speak louder so we can make a record. I want to make sure the interpreters can hear you. So we're talking about Mr. Stojic makes that decision; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was approving such taping.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course the same thing would go under Article 44 where it talks about covert photographic and video recording; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Correct -- correct -- sorry, it's my time, not your time. Don't worry. Correction to the transcript. On page 32, line 3, reference is here written to Article 17. I think it should be 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, 43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if Mr. Stojic -- if SIS, for instance, decided that they wanted to tape record or photograph or videotape the president of the HVO or any member of the HVO, Mr. Stojic would be the one to make that authorisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe you could have mentioned a better example. I'm not sure that he was in charge of approving it at that level, although from what it says here he could have decided even to tape President Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at P 00098. P 00098. And when you look at -- and while you're looking at that -- once you have it, let me know. I have a couple of questions before I to ask you about the document.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was this document shown to you by Mr. Stojic?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw several requests. I'm not sure that this was one of them. I saw several similar requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be 100 per cent sure that this is one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you met with him to discuss your expertise did he by any chance talk to you about his involvement in the financing of these sorts of matters? Financing of the military.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. This claim by my honourable colleague is just completely senseless. Mr. Karnavas is asking did the counsel for Mr. Stojic show you any documents showing -- indicating his participation in the financing. This aggressive attitude by Mr. Karnavas shows -- first of all, wastes too much time, and now he's even starting to accuse. So first of all, I need to protect Mr. Stojic because what Mr. Karnavas just said, I believe, is totally inappropriate: "Did Mr. Stojic's counsel show you the documents showing Mr. Stojic's activities regarding the financing of the HVO?" I'm only asking that we should all be correct. So if Mr. Karnavas is trying to indicate that what Mr. Prlic signed was part of a collective decision that he might be as professional to make the same claim for Mr. Stojic because Mr. Stojic was also the head of a collective body. So we cannot have two different attitudes here. That's why I need to object to this particular method of questioning, and I also need to object to the additional time approved because then I will need to have additional time in the future because just as you said, if I have two binders, the Prosecution will have four. So I will also need additional time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just need to make a correction in the transcript. I believe this is necessary for Mr. Karnavas behalf and also for Your Honours. On page 33, line 25, it is stated that Madam Nozica said that Mr. Karnavas wastes too much time. She, however, put it in different phrase. She said that with his aggressive attitude Mr. Karnavas is trying to get more time from the Chambers for his cross-examination. And given that this particular remark regards also the attitude of the Chambers, I would kindly ask you to take this into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may briefly respond --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, if there is a translation, let me say -- let me say the reason the Chamber granted time to Mr. Karnavas has nothing to do with whether or not he's being aggressive. Given Madam Nozica's objection, the witness had access to all of the documents in the archives that he consulted. Perhaps he saw certain documents relating to financial matters proving that certain individuals were involved in the financing, and perhaps in the archives was to be found the document that we have before us here; and therefore Mr. Karnavas has found it in asking the question have you seen this document, and if you've seen it, what can you say about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you go over this document with Mr. Stojic himself, sir, or any other document, for that matter?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Stojic for 15 minutes altogether in my entire life, so I did not go through any documents with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and is this the first time you see this document? If we look at it, sir, this is a --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. This is a request for opening a non-residential account. We see Mr. Stojic's name and signature. We see Mr. Jelavic's signature. Mr. Jelavic was -- held at some point the position that Mr. Stojic held, when Mr. Stojic was in Grude, when he was in logistics; correct? That's the position that Ante Jelavic held?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ante Jelavic was in charge of the logistics at the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's what Mr. Bruno Stojic was in charge of too when he was located in Grude, the same place that Mate Boban had his headquarters; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please explain that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the question is this and you make reference to it in your report at that Mr. Stojic was head of the logistics of the HVO before he became the head of the Department of Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that -- in the logistics centre, in the logistics centre was located in Grude; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Mate Boban is from Grude and his offices were in Grude; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was born in Grude, and I believe his office was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now -- we see one other signature under number 5, and then we see somebody has sign for Mate Boban. Do you see that where it says, "za"? It means for. Do you see it? And if you look at that signature and look at number 1, Bruno Stojic's signature, do we not see that Mr. Stojic has signed for Mr. Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This signature is rather similar to the signature in line 1 that was signed by Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But we don't see signatures for the head of the finance department or the president of the HVO HZ HB for this non-residential account; correct? For the opening of this non-residential account.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Finally, if we go to a couple of documents, P 00586. This is dated 17 October 1992. We see this document is on principles of organisation of the Defence Department. Have you had a chance to look at this, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that when you look at it there is no mentioning of the HVO HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document -- just a second, and I will be able to confirm that. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And did you have a chance to look at it beforehand, to make a determination whether this was actually being applied?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the decision on the basic principles of the organisation, and on the basis of this decision Mr. Stojic signed a Decision on the Organisation of the Department of Defence. This document was dated the 15th of September, although we can see here the 17th of October is the date, possibly that was the delivery date. I can say that the document that followed that was made on the basis of this document regulates certain issues differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look at P 02477. This is the Decision on the Internal Organisation of the Defence Department dated 20 May 1993. Surely you must have been given this document and shown this document; correct? Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at the last page we see again the same signature that we saw on that non-residential account, very similar to both what was for Mr. Boban and what was for Mr. Stojic. We also see a signature by Mate Boban. Here we see his actual signature. If we look at this document again, sir, there is no mentioning of the HVO HZ HB, is there?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2477? I should have it here. In this document HVO HZ HB is mentioned in item 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And how are they mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This item refers to the defence administrations, and in paragraph II it says that chiefs of defence administration are appointed by the HVO of the HZ HB following the proposal by the head of defence. I believe this is the only time that the HVO HZ HB is mentioned in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I may say that also in the preamble the HZ HB is maybe mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It talks about the president of the HVO, and it talks about the Croatian Community as opposed to the HVO HZ HB. Very well. All right. Your Honours, I appreciate the extra time being given to me. I have no further questions for this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in that case, it is time for the break. It's 10.30. We will have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: On the concept use by Judge Antonetti earlier on "competence qualifiees [phoen]," the closest equivalent we've come up with is "qualified powers." Or sometimes mandatory duty. It means a decision which taken by somebody which has to be taken because certain conditions are met.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, just one very brief matter for the record. This morning we were handed by my learned friend Mr. Scott a further Prosecution motion regarding the Bozic issue. Just on the record, on the bench are -- is the Defence response to that. It's just been filed and my learned friends have been served with a hard copy of it just before Your Honours came in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. I think Mr. Praljak will be doing the questioning. General Praljak, the floor is yours. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Marijan.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Due to the shortness of time, I formulated some questions that will be very easy to answer, so for the mentioned reasons of time, please are as concise as possible in your answers. Could we see Exhibit P 00502 on the screens, please. While we're waiting, let me ask you the following question: The assistant brigade commander for SIS, did he report the brigade commander about his work as well as the SIS headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was his duty to do so, both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find any document stating that he would send a document about that to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assistant brigade commander was not in a position to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did the assistant commander of the zone of operation for SIS also collect these reports from the brigades and report to the commander of the zone of operation as well as the SIS headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it should have been like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you find any report submitted by the assistant for SIS in a zone of operation that was submitted to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell for sure. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. That is sufficient. Did you find any report made by the SIS headquarters reporting to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same question. I'm not sure I saw anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do -- does the same apply to the military police? Did you find any documents stating or would show that the military police reports to Main Staff about its activities?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let us look at the document. The first two pages matter, namely the structure of the Main Staff. You may have seen them before. So let me ask you whether according to the organisational structure of the Main Staff there were any position forces or the military police, respectively?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document from 1992, I believe, does not contain what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do take a look at the first two pages, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, it seems that we have not been given these documents. Am I correct, or something has gone wrong on the way? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Since this document already has an exhibit number, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, you're sure aware that we cannot work on the basis of sheer numbers. We have decided that we want the paper, and maybe it is in some other -- in one of the files that we have already, but we have requested this, and we would like also to obtain it. Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is customary that documents are not repeated if some documents were submitted to the Chamber in the direct examination. So this document should be in the set of documents submitted by the Stojic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Nozica, can you indicate where it is if it is with your documents, and if so, where we can find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it is there, but I didn't show it, as far as I remember. I believe it is there. I will make an effort to find it. I believe that our expert has found it because we had it in the binder in the proofing. I'm sorry, this is -- I don't have the right to address you now, but could you tell the Chamber which document this is in the binder so as to enable the Judges to find it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it is the tenth document in binder 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, I suppose you had a talk with General Praljak before he does the questioning. I think that you knew he had the intent of referring to some documents. You should have before the hearing have made copies of the documents because look at all the papers I have behind me. Look at this. So that means that we have to go fishing for documents. Of course Mr. Praljak could say this document is in binder number 2, et cetera, but we have an issue with this. But let's move on. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] This is my mistake, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, in the document -- in this document that you surely know, mentions a position in the organisation of the Main Staff for SIS or the police.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document dated 18 September 1992, does not have such positions in the establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In possible -- after possible changes of the organisational structure of the Main Staff did you find any positions for the SIS or the military police?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen the second document about the organisational structure of the Main Staff. I know for sure that there was no position for the military police. A few days after you were relieved from your duty, I know that there were two SIS officers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know that the headquarters of the military police daily issued a bulletin about their work and distributed it to about 15 addresses in Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen that bulletin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now about the document you saw yesterday. We don't have to put it on the screen. This is 2D 00944, dated 19/11/93, in which mention is made of a certain Mr. Bandic in the Main Staff. We saw that document yesterday, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there was another desk officer, but there was also Mr. Bandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's stick to Mr. Bandic. Based on that document, obviously, in your report, in paragraph 39, toward the end of the paragraph, you state the following: "At the -- in the HVO Main Staff an assistant for SIS was no longer envisaged by establishment in 1992."

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: "In the latter half of 1993, such a position must have exist." I'm interested in this phrase "must have existed." What is the likelihood with which you can claim, based on the document dated 19/11/93 that there was a position in the latter half of 1992? Or to put it differently was he appointed two days earlier, five days earlier, a year earlier, and what does this "must have" mean? Is that certain or probable?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I refer here to a document dated 2nd of September, 1993. I don't know whether it is here, and that is the approval of the appointment of some officers. I cannot say off the top of my head who it was, but there were several names. And then there is this later document that you mentioned which can be interpreted either way, as you correctly say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, have you ever seen the appointment of that person to the Main Staff, the appointment, a document of appointment?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember having seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So can we draw the conclusion by which I will finish that since you have not seen the appointment and since the position is not -- does not exist in the organisational structure, which need not be particularly significant, though, that you cannot state or claim with certainty that he was there in the latter half of 1993? You can suppose with some degree of probability that he was there, but you could not claim, certainly not for certain, that that was actually the case. Do you agree with me that this would be a logical conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right to a great extent. I do not remember this document. I refer to the document dated 2 September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's a document about -- which is a proposal, and there is no document showing the appointment, so we cannot be sure that, at least during the time while Praljak was there at the Main Staff, there was a person in charge of SIS. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would reformulate the sentence to say that in the latter half of 1993, such a person was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you think so, or do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know based on that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Which document?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents dated 19/11/93. In the Main Staff there is a SIS officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That is a sort of weird logic. He may have been appointed on the 16th of November. Please read the -- through the entire document. What makes you draw the conclusion that the person was not there half a year earlier or a year earlier? And even if a document says that he was there, which doesn't necessarily mean that it's indeed the case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Praljak. That is not a bad will of mine, but now you are asking the witness to read a document which is not on the screen, which is -- I have not found anywhere, and this really is not the way to work here. Perhaps you can help me out. I would be grateful. Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] 2D 00944, 2D 00944.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, please, where it says as of which time that person should have been there in this document. Show meet sentence from which you draw the conclusion that the person was there in the latter half of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may help. That document is in my binder, in the middle -- in the middle of binder 1. So if I can -- if this is helpful for the witness or the Chamber. It may be the 15th document or so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, the sentence you read out to me a minute ago, I refer to the document dated the 2nd of September about the appointment to the Main Staff. I don't have that document here, but it isn't by chance that I refer to this document. I don't know what it says by heart, but it mentioned eight or nine names. That can be easily found out. And you are now confronting me with a document dated 19/11. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That document was shown yesterday, and based on that document you said that he was there in the latter half of 1993. Even that document from September is not the latter half of 1993.
