And that document is not an appointment but possibly a proposal, but we don't have that document here so we can't discuss it. So you see, I don't want to dwell on this topic any longer. My answer is completely satisfactory -- or your answer is completely satisfactory to me, and I thank you for it. This concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the accuracy of the transcript, the witness in his report refers to a document dated 2/9/93, and that document 2D 00928. That document is -- is admitted as evidence. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] That document is -- does not contain the same names. Some people were there, then they went away, and then some other people came, and this -- that's from where you draw the conclusion of that person being there in the latter half of 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I got it right, all the Defence counsels have taken the floor. So it is now Ms. Alaburic's turn.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not all the Defence teams have cross-examined yet, such as the Coric Defence, and they will be coming after me. Your Honours, I'd like to say good morning to everyone in the courtroom, to my learned friends and to Mr. Marijan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In these proceedings, I'm going to cross-examine you on behalf of General Petkovic, who is my client and also on behalf of General Praljak who ceded part of his time to the Petkovic Defence. I'd like to inform the Trial Chamber and also you, Mr. Marijan that for the most part I'm going to deal with the topic of the relationship between the head of the Defence Department and the armed forces of the HZ HB, and the relationship between the head of -- I'm repeating for the transcript the head of the Defence Department and the armed forces of the HZ HB. And if I have time left over, I'm going to ask you some questions in order to clarify some of your answers. For example, the questions raised by Judge Trechsel because I consider that those were important questions and that we owe a fuller explanation in response to them. Now, the provisions that I'm going to use and regulations are to be found in the Defence binder, the Stojic Defence binder, which my learned friend Ms. Nozica put an X to. It was binder X. And those will be documents P 586, the Decision on the Establishment of the Defence Department [Realtime transcript read in error, "company"], and I'm going to deal with item 9 first and foremost which His Honour Judge Antonetti quite rightly qualified as the most important provision. Let me repeat, the title was -- because it wasn't properly recorded in the transcript, it is the Decision to Establish the Organisational Structure of the Defence Department. It's not Defence company, it's Defence department. Yes, Defence Department. That's right. And the following regulations will be the regulations governing the armed forces, number P 289 from May 1992 -- July 1992, and P 588, dated October 1992. Now, my binder has been ordered in the following way: The documents are in the order in which I'll be showing them. Mr. Marijan, it is not my aim, at least not in this first set of documents, to discuss the contents of those documents with you, but what I'm interested in is whether you were familiar with those documents. Now, to begin with let me just check my understanding of your report. If I understood you correctly and understood your report correctly, you compiled it on the basis of analysing provisions and an analysis of certain orders, decisions, minutes, records, and similar documents. Have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you have understood it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, before I start asking you my questions, I'd like an explanation. In paragraphs 119 and 120 of your report, you speak about the responsibilities and authority of the Defence Department with respect to military prison and detention centres, and those paragraphs you place in the section which is titled "Military -- compulsory military service, compulsory military service." Now, I'd like to ask you to explain to us whether this is a mistake, or did you do this intentionally in order for this to escape the reader?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a mistake. It should be employee relationships.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I have to ask you to explain that term. Do you mean it has to do with employee relations?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My microphone seems to be on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know where else I would place that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I have to repeat my question. You mentioned employee relationships. Now my question is that under that term do you imply the authority of the head of the Defence Department over prisoners of war, military prisons, military detention centres? Just give me a yes or no answer. We don't have much time to go into explanations. Just yes or no, please. Have I understood you correctly? Is that what you think?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that would be the closest.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, in view of the fact that my colleague Ms. Nozica emphasised that you're not a lawyer and you're not qualified to interpret provisions and regulations, I'm not going to ask you about regulations for the time being, but I am going to ask you about individual decisions. Now, yesterday and this is reported on page 75 of the transcript, said that the head of the Defence Department was not in the chain of command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my conclusion, yes, having conducted an analysis of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And on that same page you said that you hadn't seen a single document on the basis of which one would be able to conclude that the Defence Department was in the chain of command of armed forces. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's what I said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I'd like us to go on to the next set of documents, and please just tell me whether you knew about the document, were familiar with them, or not. And the first document is P 600. The contents of the document is not what interests us now. P 00600 is the document number. So take a look at that document in my binder. We'll take the documents in the order they've been put into the binder. Keep it in front of you because we're going to need the ELMO. So this then is a document dated the 18th of October, 1992, Bruno Stojic, and he is calling upon the commander of the Central Bosnia operative zone to a meeting. Now, tell me, did you know that Bruno Stojic had direct communication with the commanders of the operative zones and that he called them to attend meetings and quite obviously talked to them?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the document. You said we weren't to go into the contents, but, yes, those are the contents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document is P 00619. It's a report by the military police administration for the 22nd of October, 1992, and at the beginning of the second paragraph it says, and I quote: "Pursuant to an order from the [as interpreted] Defence Department and based on a decision by the Presidency of the HVO, during the day we took the following facilities in town: The post office building, the MUP centre, the police station, and we stopped the work of Radio Mostar." I'd like to make a correction in line 19. The word "head" was left out. So the sentence reads: "Pursuant to an order from the head of the Defence Department." Now, I'd like to know whether the head of the Defence Department issued such orders.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is familiar to me. That's what I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, the third document I'd like to look at is P 00799. The document is dated the 25th of November, 1992. Bruno Stojic is issuing an order to the commander of the Rama Brigade and to the commander of the Military Police Platoon in Prozor as well as to the commander of the Military Police Battalion to report to the offers of the head of the Defence Department. Now, do you know that Bruno Stojic issued such orders and had direct communication with the commanders of the brigades and also the commanders of certain military police units?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document is P 00804. The document is dated the 25th November, 1993. Once again Bruno Stojic is issuing an order to the Bruno Busic Regiment to redeploy, to be transferred. Now, do you know that Bruno Stojic issued certain units of the HVO orders of this kind?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the next document is P 01098. It is an order from Bruno Stojic, date the 11th of January, 1993. And in the lower half we see that the order was sent to the commanders of the operative zones, the commanders of the brigades, and the military police administration. And this order prohibits persons to -- in uniform and bearing arms to move around. Now, do you know that Bruno Stojic issued orders of this kind directly to the commanders of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, the next document is P 1140. It is Bruno Stojic's order of the 15th of January, 1993, and here -- well, the document -- this is a document we've seen in this courtroom quite frequently. It is a document by which Bruno Stojic orders the main -- certain activities to the Main Staff and orders the resubordination of certain units to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I don't want to go into this document in detail. We're all very familiar with it, but are you familiar with the document. Have you ever seen it before?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document is 4D 348. It is a report from Colonel Miro Andric, and we'll see what post he held, what position he held. It is directly addressed to Bruno Stojic, and in the first paragraph it says as follows: "Following a verbal order from the head of the Defence Department of the HZ HB, Mr. Bruno Stojic, on the 12th of January, 1993, I went to carry out a mission in Prozor with the objective of calming the situation in the Gornji Vakuf municipality." Tell us, please, Mr. Marijan, did you know that Bruno Stojic issued oral orders of this type and have you seen the document?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I've seen several reports from Mr. Andric. He was deputy head of the Main Staff at the time, but I cannot say with certainty that I have actually seen this document; but I have seen some of his documents whether I've seen this one I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, in view of the fact that in the transcript not -- your answer hasn't been translated. He was the deputy head of the Main Staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document, P 1316. And it's an order from Bruno Stojic to all the operative zones and military police administrations to let through the vehicles of -- carrying humanitarian aid and their convoys. Now, did you see this -- have you seen this order ever and similar ones sent to the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we looked at this document yesterday because it's included in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now look at the next document which is 2D 00984. I think that you have already seen the document and it -- that it's mentioned in your report, but let's check it out.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at document 2D 00439. It is a document dated the 20th of May, 1993, Bruno Stojic, first of all, is seeking complete data on the situation in Tuzla and Brcko, a complete report on the situation there; and then from the Zrinjski 115th Brigade, he receives an answer from the commander. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, but I would rather say yes than no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Judge's microphone be switched off, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, P 3146 is the next document. The document is one from Bruno Stojic. It is dated the 3rd of July 1993. It is sent to the Petar Kresimir Brigade in Livno or, rather, Livno. It is the brigade that you were in too; right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So Bruno Stojic here says or, rather, orders that the military police from -- that the Livno military police be relocated to Mostar. Did you know that Bruno Stojic issued such orders on the relocation of certain units of the armed forces depending on the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that question would merit a longer comment but you're asking me whether I've seen the document or not, so, yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now look at the next document which is P 05232, 05232 is the correct number. The document has the status of exhibit. It is an order from Bruno Stojic dated the 20th of September, 1993, and it says due to these newly arisen situation in Mostar, Buna, Zitomislic, and Capljina, Bruno Stojic orders that all human and material resources be engaged in all free military and civilian police forces, hunting associations and other free forces in these areas and be placed under the command of the commander of the 1st Brigade or at the time sector of the South-eastern Herzegovina operation zone that is to say Colonel Obradovic. Tell us, have you ever seen this order before?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note there is a lot of interference in the courtroom and it is difficult to hear the speaker. Thank you. It's been put right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document is 41183 a document in which Bruno Stojic directly sends the commander of the -- is sent to the commander of the brigade in Zepce. Do you know that Bruno Stojic had direct communication -- let me repeat the number of the document 4D -- 4D, D as in Dubrovnik, 1183.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you knew that Bruno Stojic had direct communication with the brigade commanders?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now let us look at one more document. These were taken at random as examples. The document is P 06364. And it is a report from the Commander Ivica Rajic directly to Bruno Stojic. You say you knew about this? Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, if I can conclude on the basis of all that, Mr. Marijan, most of these documents, almost all of them, in fact, are familiar. You have seen them before; right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the exception of that one report from Mr. Andric which I'm not sure about, I can say that I've seen all the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now tell me, please, documents have you seen other similar documents?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there's some more, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you to go back to a statement you made yesterday and recorded on page 75 of the transcript when you said that you hadn't seen a single document on the basis of which you would be able to conclude that the Defence Department was in the chain of command over the armed forces. Now, tell us, Mr. Marijan, whether you stand by that position and that conclusion of yours or on the basis of all the documents I've put to you and the others that you mentioned, you could perhaps revise your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: I can't remember with absolute certainty what came before that statement of mine, those words of mine, but when I say chain of command, I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'll go into that later. Don't tell me what you mean and imply by the chain of command. Just tell me whether you stand by the statement you made yesterday or rather the conclusion that you made yesterday, and in due course we'll go into your understanding of the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can we first analyse what I mean when I say chain of command, what I imply by that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well we're not going to analyse what you mean by chain of command. We're going to analyse what the chain of command, in fact, is. Very well. Now, in the second portion of my documents or binder beginning with the sectors in the Defence Department, look at document 4D 12 --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise but the witness has just been shown a sequence of documents, a set of documents, and I'm afraid that any comment is lacking about this series of documents; and I think the witness said at one point that one of the documents would deserve further comment so either I -- I suggest he either be asked questions on this sequence of documents, or we're going to go through documents and not come to a question because this way on the record we just have the witness saying he was familiar with the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Might I respond to my learned friend Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Alaburic, you have presented to a series of witnesses and you said well, Witness I'm presenting a number of documents that indicate such and such, et cetera and do you agree with the following conclusion that can be drawn from examining these documents; and then you go on and explain, and then the witness says, "I agree," or, "I don't agree." Well, I think it might have been useful to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I only wanted to evaluate the statement that the witness made that he had not seen any document which would include the head of the Department of Defence into the chain of command. I believe that on the basis of these documents we can make a different conclusion, and I simply wanted to check whether the witness was familiar with these documents or not. We now know that the witness did see these documents, so the question is simply whether he stands by his conclusion that the head of department, Bruno Stojic, was still not within the chain of command or not; and the witness said that first of all we should discuss what the witness -- what the chain of command actually means. So given that this is my cross-examination, please allow me now in the continuation to talk about that chain of command, and I would kindly ask my learned colleague Ms. Nozica to stick to the procedure, rules of procedure, and if she has any objection to any question to object in appropriate time nobody interfered with her questioning, so I would kindly ask her not to interfere with her colleague's.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no need to be nervous. I am not interfering with anybody. I understood very well what Madam Alaburic just said. She showed a range of documents to see whether the witness will stand by his statement that Mr. Stojic was within the chain of command or not. I simply lacked that question. And just as Madam Alaburic said it is her conclusion that he was within the chain of command, but I believe that neither her nor my conclusion are relevant for this Court but, rather, the conclusions made by the witness, and this is why I interfered; but I will try to keep my interferes as least as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour, we will come back to this conclusion after the next set of documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you please now look at the scheme 4D 128, and I would kindly ask the usher to put this on the ELMO. I would like to thank our law assistant, Mr. Lazic, who prepared this one and a range of other schemes that we prepared for you, Mr. Marijan. So this -- the document 4D 1280. Mr. Marijan, this is something that we prepared for you in order to be able to go very quickly through certain issues without losing too much time on reading the documents, interpreting them and so on. Could you please take a look at the schematic. It should show various bodies of Herceg-Bosna at the level of the entire Herceg-Bosna which had certain powers over the defence. This document was prepared on the basis of the Decree on the Armed Forces, and the structure, the organisational structure of the Defence Department was made on the basis of the document P 586, and I believe that everything that you testified about in the past two days, and that is included into your report, is included into the schematic as well. If you, however, can find any mistakes, please take a pen and cross out whatever you believe needs to be cross out.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that this organisational structure has been presented very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The copy that you have on the ELMO, could you please put your signature and today's date on it, and I would kindly ask an IC number for this document.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] I can sign it anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document will shall be given Exhibit IC 00904. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Before we go into any further details, Mr. Marijan, can we just repeat some things which I believe are very important. Yesterday you stated that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I intervened. There's something I don't quite understand. In your binder, Ms. Alaburic, this document figures under 4D 01280, and now you are asking an IC number for it. Which of the two? Normally there should not be two numbers for the same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is there a possibility that the witness will intervene with some of these schematics. This is why we wanted to have a 4D number for the schematics prepared by us and an IC number for the schematic on which the witness made some corrections or if he -- even if he did not make any corrections with his signature he shows that he approves with such a schematic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I can -- I can follow. One doesn't do it with documents. One could with the same logic one could say every document the witness says, "I've seen it," ask him to put a signature. Isn't it a bit of loss of time and an unnecessary formality which also may lead to confusion with having two numbers for the same document? I would suggest that we do not proceed in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honour. I fully accept your suggestion, and this is why I shall continue as follows: If the witness believes that a schematic is incorrect and he makes an intervention, then I will ask for an IC number for that particular schematic. So I will give up on my request for an IC number for this particular schematic and once again I'm very grateful for this useful comment by Judge Trechsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And I -- I appreciate you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I appreciate your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, you told us yesterday that a sector assistants were directly responsible to the head of Department of Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you explained what were the tasks of particular sectors belonging to the Department of Defence. So we can conclude that this fell under the remit of the assistants.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We could see that apart from the tasks mentioned here from your report it results that the Department of Defence also had certain other powers, for example, when it comes to military prisoners and prisoners of war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that none of these provisions mentioned the position of the POWs, but certain -- given that there are certain characteristic documents by Mr. Stojic, there is also the Decision on the Establishment of Military Prisons.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So apart from the Decision on the Organisational Structure of the Sectors, there are some other regulations regulating different tasks of the Department of Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are several other regulations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, does this mean that there are certain issues falling under the military law area that have also been included into the remit of the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember having seen any regulations including that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Given that Their Honours are very familiar with this, I would not like to waste any time on this. Let us now try to analyse the decision on basic principles of the Department of Defence. This is binder X and the document is P 586, and point 9, which just as His Honour Judge Antonetti said is crucial for the topic of your report. You have this decision in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm particularly interested, and I would kindly ask you to give us your understanding, because your understanding, regardless of whether you are qualified to provide a legal interpretation or not, your answer will enable us to evaluate properly your report. So please give us your understanding of the last two paragraphs of the item 9. I will quote the first of these paragraph: "Within the remit of the specific authorities of the president of the HZ HB, the head of the Department of Defence is subordinated to" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise, but we do not see this document, so if the counsel could kindly read again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So: "Within the remit of the concrete and specific tasks of the president of the HZ HB the chief of Main Staff is superior to the command of the HVO." Could you kindly give us your interpretation of this provision.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe -- first of all, I would like to determine the time when this was made.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please do not. Please give us your understanding of this provision. So the Chief of the Main Staff, in which parts is he superior to the command of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Chief of the Main Staff is superior to the command of the HVO when it comes to some specific and concrete powers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Given to him by whom?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given to him by the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. That is Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, the Chief of the Main Staff, could he do anything else apart from this general and specific powers given by the president of the HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, he shouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the beginning of this provision. Can the Chief of the Main Staff do any things for which he would respond to the head of the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you see -- take a look at the beginning of item 9.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought this is what you had in mind. Well, here in this item 9 we have a list of issues for which the Chief of the Main Staff responds to the head of the Department of Defence. We can see it in the third paragraph. So my understanding is this is what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So I will repeat my question: Can the Chief of the Main Staff carry out any tasks for which he's not authorised by the president of the HZ HB but for which he would be authorised by, for example, the head of Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from what you've just read to me, I can conclude that the Chief of the Main Staff only carries out the tasks that he's authorised to carry out by the president of the HZ HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, there is no word "only "anywhere here. It only says that in these issues the Chief of the Main Staff will be superior to the command of the Croatian Defence Council. So one of the techniques for interpretation of legal texts is that in all other issues, the Chief of the Main Staff is not superior to the command of the HVO. Although you're not qualified to interpret the law, could you tell us whether you've heard of such a possibility and whether such an interpretation would be agreeable to you?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that I've heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we take a look at the following paragraph, which is directly linked to the previous one, and it says: "The brigade commanders shall be subordinated and responsible to the president of the HZ HB as the Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces and to the head of the Defence Department and Chief of the Main Staff within the scope of their responsibilities in accordance with the powers described above." Mr. Marijan, let us see what is your interpretation of this provision. Does it follow from this provision that the brigade commanders always and in everything are subordinated and responsible to the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna as the Commander-in-Chief?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we could conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude that at lower levels, the responsible people are either the head of the Defence Department or the Chief of the Main Staff depending on the issue at hand or, rather, whether a question comes within the remit of the head of the Defence department or whether it comes within the remit of the Chief of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, looking at all -- the whole of this item, the upper part of the paragraph, they are -- and from this, it does not follow that they are responsible to the head of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, I'm asking you this at the level of literacy, general literacy without any legal interpretation. The sentence begins: "The brigade commanders shall be subordinate and responsible to the president of the HZ HB," and then it says, "and to the head and chief of the main -- head of the Defence Department, Chief of the Main Staff within the scope of their responsibilities." Now my concrete question is are the brigade commanders subordinate and responsible to the head of the Defence Department according to his remit?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they are, yes. So my answer is yes. Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right fine now we're going to try and look -- see that together to see what actually happened in practice, to take a look at that together. And look at the next schematic which relates to the Health Sector the document is 4D 1285. And I'd like the document to be placed on the ELMO as well, please. The schematic was compiled on the basis of the Stojic Defence, which you -- on their documents. We just added the operative zones because in that document they have been left out. So would you now take a look at that document and either confirm this structure for the health centre or make any corrections if you feel that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that I can say here, my only comment as far as the Health Sector is concerned, is that what is lacking here is the assistant, assistant head of the health department. So I think the chiefs of the Medical Corps and so on would come under him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you write that in? Put "Assistant," and then draw the connecting lines that you think apply?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You now linked one of the services to him, the care service.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The care service to the assistant.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't do that. I linked the Medical Corps and the units in the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So you mean the blue part?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Then link that blue section directly to the assistant.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in keeping with our agreement, may we have an IC number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not going to interrupt my colleague, but there's been a request from my client. We have this schematic only in English on our screens, and I think it would be a better idea --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the ELMO is in Croatian. It's in Croatian on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Fine. I apologise, but that request came in from my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica [as interpreted], I'm a bit lost, because earlier on you requested the document be given an IC number and the Chamber asked the registrar to give that number. I think it was 904. My colleague took the floor to point out to you that there was an issue because this number had already been given, and there could be a confusion regarding these two numbers. So the Chamber decided to withdraw that number. Now there's 4D 1285, 4D 1285. So there is already a number, but now you want an IC number, so I no longer understand. Fine. Since there is a change, a new number is provided. But when -- or during the deliberations on the judgement, we'll have to juggle with all the documents, so we'll give an IC number, but, registrar you have to remove the first number 904, if I'm not mistaken and give 904 to that particular document and we have to juggle all the time between the two.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, in line with your decision, this current document shall now be assigned Exhibit IC 00904. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, you made this intervention just now because, if I understood you correctly, what you wanted to say is this: That the parts of the Defence Department in the Health Sector which were within the armed forces -- I apologise. Let me repeat the question. I didn't formulate it properly. That parts of the Medical Corps, the Medical Corps service in the armed forces, had direct communication with the assistant head of the Defence Department for health; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My intervention was as follows and should be understood in the following way: I didn't deal with the Health Sector in any great detail because as far as I understood it the then-assistant will be coming in, but it's not logical judging on all similar solutions, that is to say the security service, how that is set up, or morale or moral guidance to link -- we're dealing with the head of the Medical Corps of the operative zone, I mean it's logical that he is linked to the assistant.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What is important for me now, Mr. Marijan, is for us to try and see the direct communication between the Health Sector and the armed forces, that line. So look at document P 4145, the next document now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Alaburic. I would like to have something clarified. Witness, Mr. Marijan, you have also struck out the line that connected the care service for the wounded and it's chief to the -- what I will call blue zone, for simplification. Have I understood at that correctly? According to you, it's not the case that this chief of care service was responsible for the blue sector, but it was the deputy from Ocnic [phoen] of the assistant for the health, the chief assistant for health?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, well, we're dealing with logic here and looking at the logics in the security service in the Political Activities Department and so on that where the commanders or assistant chiefs in the operative zones from the Defence Department who have their headquarters or something like that, that they are responsible to the assistant head for that particular sector and not some other service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Witness. I must strictly and strongly contradict. We are not dealing nor interested in logic. We want to know what was actually the case, and if you make a guess based on a logical conclusion, then it is a guess, and it is not testimony on a fact. I hope that the distinction is clear. So what are the facts, not what would logically be the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, my colleague is quite right. We're here to ascertain facts and not theories and precisely since you wear two hats: You're an expert and you're in the field. So you're best placed to understand the question I'm about to ask. I can see that according to this document in operation areas brigades had their own physicians, and you will tell us in your brigade there was a physician? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the brigade had a number of doctors within the Medical Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. The brigade has several physicians. Imagine perhaps you were involved in combat activities. Imagine that you need to make arrangements in case soldiers get wounded to provide treatment to soldiers who are wounded during combatting activities. If the brigade commander realises that the number of doctors available is not sufficient, I presume that in the traditional chain of command, he will ask the operational area commander for support so that other areas, possibly present in the area, provide their doctors. But imagine that there is a shortage of either doctors or ambulances. Will the commander of the operational area call the deputy of the ministry of defence in charge of health to tell him that there will be an operation in three days' time, We're going to deploy 3.000 men. It's like that we will have casualties, wounded or dead, and we lack medical logistical resources. Could you make sure that some support is provided to us? And in such a case is it the deputy in the yellow square here making that decision? It is a specific example I'm putting to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, that's how things should be and that's how things must be. So in this case of a brigade not having enough men or the Medical Corps not having the resources needed to tackle the situation on the battleground, then the chief of the Medical Corps asks assistance and reinforcement from his superior, the head of the Medical Corps in the operative zone. But if he can't respond, then it goes further and assistance is sought from the Medical Corps Sector -- or, rather, the Health Sector because they have these services.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. I agree with what you say. This is sheer military logic, but have you seen documents showing that such situations actually arose which would substantiate the diagram we have in front of us between the blue and the yellow, or is this just a theoretical diagram and you have not seen yourself an instance of this? Please allow the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission I have a document here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hold on, Mrs. Alaburic. I'm asking a question which has to do with credibility which is very important, so don't disturb him and let him answer. My question is very straight forward. What we have this flow chart, you have the schematic of the chain of command, and I'm asking him if he's seen documents demonstrating that at some stage the commander of the operational area asked the deputy of the Department of Defence for logistical support. The answer would be yes. What is your answer, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mrs. Alaburic, before we started this discussion, opened a document which is the reverse of the situation. It doesn't go from the operative zone up to the sector but the other way round, from the sector down. It's this feedback mechanism. So this was an example which can illustrate the point and support it. And I have to say that I didn't deal with the Medical Corps much. Military matters were what I focus on, but I know this from my own experience, although at the time I was within the operative zone and I know that that's how we function, that hierarchy was respected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Mrs. Alaburic, I give you the floor, and you could perhaps complement this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't want to interfere in the witness's answer to your question. I just wanted to draw your attention to the fact that we are going to look at a number of documents to deal with this, but before we go into them just tell me, Mr. Marijan, the diagram that we just looked at, does it correspond to the diagram 2D 00752 which you used in compiling your report and to which you refer in the footnotes? It looks different in graphical terms, but organisationally speaking is what I'm asking you about. If you don't know what I mean and can't see the diagram in your mind now -- you don't remember it? 2D, do you, that particular one?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You mean the previous diagram?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: From the Stojic Defence, the diagram that you used in preparing your report. But let's move on as we haven't got much time, unfortunately, document P 4145 is the next one I'd like us to look at, and it speaks of direct communication between the assistant head of the Defence Department and the armed forces. I'm not interested for the moment in the contents of the document. All I'm interested in is whether you can confirm that the Health Sector had direct communication with the services -- the health services in the operative zones and other units.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that is evident from this document, especially to whom it is addressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, the next document is P 1417, and it is an order from Bruno Stojic, dated February 1993, and it relates to missing persons and captured persons sent to the operative zone commanders and chief of the Medical Corps in the brigades and operative zones, and apart from Bruno Stojic it was signed by his assistant, Bagaric. Now, does this document confirm direct communication between the Defence Department and the brigades when it comes to the Medical Corps, Medical Corps issues?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Next document, P 1428. Again Bagaric and Stojic direct communication within the zones of operation and brigades. This document also confirms the existence of their communication. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we were to try and define the chain of command in the area of health in accordance with paragraph 9 of the Decree on the Internal Organisation of the Department of Defence, would we be right to say that the health service is within the remit of the Department of Defence and that brigade commanders with respect to that were accountable to the head of the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the latter part of your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that health is within the remit of the head of the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a -- no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that health is not within the remit of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In terms of the establishment, the organisational structure.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in -- in those terms, I believe no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we look at paragraph 9 about the Decree on the Internal Organisation Structure of the Department of Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mrs. Alaburic. I find at least in the translation I heard the last answer a bit ambivalous, because you say, "In those terms I believe no." What do you mean exactly in those terms? In other terms, yes, and in which other terms yes then? I would be grateful if you could clarify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would have to take a look at the diagram showing the structure of the Main Staff, but I don't remember at the time the chief of Main Staff does have an establishment position of a head of Medical Corps, but Ms. Alaburic was asking about health, and health falls within the remit of the Department of Defence, because it is actually a sector of the department. The question was about the Main Staff, and I was thinking about the armed forces, hence the doubt, but I believe Ms. Alaburic will arrive at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have the document before me. I have another question. Did you yourself participate in combat where your comrades were killed? Did it occur? And the only point of my question -- my following question is if you answer that one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, yes, I did, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that you said yes. When that occurred, when your comrades were killed during combat, did you see a doctor come in to examine the individual and determine that they had indeed died? Were you familiar with that? Did you have knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, one of the better organise components of the HVO was the Medical Corps. I believe that they received awards and were considered extraordinary in global terms when it comes to their efficiency. During any instance of combat, there was a medical man or a paramedic in every platoon. But to return to your question directly, the head of the Medical Corps of any brigade had to confirm death, whichever way inflicted, in combat or any other way, and then a report would be drafted, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you. I was asking that question because the document which is quite clear and which comes from the Department of Defence signed by Mr. Stojic instructs all operational personnel that if there is any suspicion of criminal activity, that they must do an autopsy on the body, et cetera. So that is the meaning of the document as I read it, and, therefore, you have confirmed to me that when combat occurred without there necessarily being any criminal activity, in any case, when combat occurred the doctor would examine the bodies. Fine. This is -- this is clear. Madam, we're going to have a break in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, let us try to sum up what we said about the health service. We said that health service issues were within the remit of the Department of Defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: To the extent that you can remember now, in terms of establishment, the Main Staff didn't have a representative of the health service?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's easy to verify, but I don't remember it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let -- let us suppose that the Main Staff didn't have the medical service, and if we go back to paragraph 9 to -- of the decree on the basic principles of the organisation of the Department of Defence, can we say that the brigade commander in -- for health-related issues was accountable to the head of the Department of Defence because health services were within his remit?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we can say as much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us continue with the Morale Sector. Take a look at the diagram of document 4D 1284.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us have this on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, take a look, and I believe that this is an accurate representation in accordance with the documents mentioned below. First and foremost, the documents of the Defence of Bruno Stojic. But if you should find any inaccuracies, please point them out.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never been very happy with most diagrams I've seen. In this blue block there is an issue with subordination and hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is unclear. This may be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I can clarify. There is a direct link from the left side entering the brigade from the vertical lines and to the zone of operation because in accordance with the documents that you used and read out to us here the assistant commanders for morale in the brigades and zones of operation were appointed in the Department of Defence.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were appointed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And lower-rank commanders in battalions and companies were appointed differently, and therefore there is no direct link between the lower rank units with the Morale Sector. Instead, the link is established vertically through the brigades and the zones of operation. Mr. Marijan, if you cannot comment on this diagram, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have drawn this differently, but okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You can look at this it during the break and cross out everything you think needs to be and then we'll get back to it. Let's now take a look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the best thing is that we have the break now. It's now 12.30. We shall have 20 minutes' break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two pieces of information. As to the summaries, the Chamber will file a written decision this afternoon, so you will here about this decision this afternoon. As to time, Mrs. Alaburic, you have used 51 minutes, meaning that you have another 39 minutes, and you should be able to complete your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may remind you that General Praljak has not used 30 minutes. He used 12 minutes, which means that I can take his 18 minutes, and together with my 39 that makes the -- a total, whichever it is, 57.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that by the end of this trial we'll all have very strong maths, that is for sure. If Mr. Praljak gives you these unused minutes, you have another 57 minutes, which means that you will not finish today. But, Mr. Kovacic, do you confirm that you have given your time to Ms. Alaburic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I believe I mentioned that before Praljak started, that what he would not use, it belongs to Ms. Alaburic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. It's in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Perhaps it is judicious to recall that this will be quite exceptional, because the Chamber has decided not to accept more dealings between Defence teams; but for today, in view of the fact that you had a great demand and were cut brutally to what you have got, the Chamber decided has decided the present, but I should just warn that this should not become a rule again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the colleague took the floor probably because he thinks that the guide-lines are different on this, but anyway, thank you, Your Honours, for letting me use General Praljak's time. And as I'm in favour of the proverb, "Hope lives as long as I live," I will -- I hope to get a few minutes additionally if I should need it then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a bit of a mystery. Mr. Karnavas had used 15 minutes extra. I do not know where they come from. I thought I understood that they had been given to him by Mr. Praljak. So it must be the Holy Ghost. I don't know where these 15 minutes come from. And I asked Mr. Karnavas. You said yes, these 15 minutes were given to you, but I forgot to ask who had given you these 15 minutes, but let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may remind you of the intervention of my learned friend Ms. Nozica who, like I, understood that you allotted additional time to Mr. Karnavas, and he was allotted due to his aggressive approach. I do not have an aggressive approach, but I hope that you will be lenient to me also.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a rule the Chamber only grants time taken away from others, because we ourselves do not have a time capital to give away. You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, I saw that you raised your hand to say something.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did wanted -- want to ask the Chamber about a problem. It's been repeatedly said to me that I'm not a lawyer, which is a fact; but I do know something about the army, and for a long time I dealt with an army for things were clear, where terminology was clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I ask for permission for that what the witness is saying now is not counted against my time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will not be counted against you, but please move on. What did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sure that in the continuation of this trial there will be a lot of misunderstanding, which stems from the organisation of the HVO and the way they drew up their regulatory acts and documents. There are very few of them, I must point out, and in comparison to other armies, they are the worst in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia. And in the HVO did not have its own military terminology at all. I would like to point out one example. In the Decree on the Armed Forces of Herceg-Bosna, there is paragraph 29. We don't have to look at it at all. I will tell you what it says. It deals with the powers of the president of the HZ HB, and for command the term "leadership" is used, and this term, "leadership," has never been defined, and if it had been maybe now I wouldn't have a problem with this story of the chain of command. Because if we take this to the extreme, I could say that I've never seen the definition a zone of operation. I can only suppose what it is. I have never seen the definition of an HVO brigade. I can suppose what it is based on my knowledge of other things. But I know the former Yugoslav army, and from -- there is a term which was banned from Croatian glossaries and probably also from glossaries of Herceg-Bosna because the term was deemed Serbian although it certainly isn't. Each and every document that was shown to me these days that read order and Yugoslav terminology not only that of the federal army but also in the terminology of the republics, it would be something else. It would be another word, "naredba." That can also be translated as "order." And what -- so the word "zapovijed," that was used, and I always link with combat activity. This has to do with my background. And some of the these terminological issues seem to undermine my credibility. It isn't only about terminology though, yesterday, I mentioned some things that -- even today I can see that Mr. Scott is absent because he's been working on these trials longest. We still don't know who appoints the chief of General Staff, and some other things are unclear. So I with like to make clear to the Chamber that I'm dealing with an area here that is poorly defined. And another example that was shown to me yesterday, and I understood what Mr. Karnavas wanted, in the decree of the president of the HZ HB, date the 15th of September, where there is no HVO, you will find a completely different definition of some concepts. I have never had the impression reading the documents that never anybody asked themselves the question why there is lack of consistency, why things have been skip. Some things were, rather, left out. The HVO never really had a military lawyer. I'm not sure whether the Chamber understands what I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've perfectly understood. Thank you for sharing this with us and pointing our attention to the terms used in all the documents from the HVO. According to you, those who drafted those documents are not highly qualified lawyers, and there were former Yugoslavia attacks and on account of terms used, someone wanted to change this using the Croatian language, for it is possible that some terms may be inaccurate. This is what I understand from what you said. And as far as I know, you were lucky or unlucky to have to give evidence in trials. And since you must already have realised that beforehand, why did you not say that in the previous trial in which you were a witness? And in your conclusion, you should have said, These are the important terms, and you provide examples. Why did you not do that? This is not criticism. What I'm saying is that what you just said is important. Why have you not written this down? Now it's in the transcript, but it would have been better had it been in the report. We got the point. At least I got the point. We'll take that into account when reviewing documents, but whenever you come across such problems please point it out -- point them out to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, Your Honour, but when I was here for the first time the topic was different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Ms. Alaburic, taking into account what has just been said, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Marijan, thank you for these observations, and do point it out to us if you think that terminology is wrong or something is badly phrased. Were you able to look at the diagram of the Morale Sector during the break and do you have comments?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, think it would be best to draw this anew. There are too many lines, I believe, in principle, although I do not suppose there was ill-will involved. So it would have been better if the line did not go through the administration because this way, you can get the impression that these three administrations of the Morale Sector are superior to the assistant commanders in the units; and we can go back to the appointment and then you know who was accountable to who. So this -- the assistant commanders down there are clearly not accountable to these here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So what you are referring to is drawn the way it is because that's exactly how it was depicted in document 2D 685. It's a document from the Stojic Defence, and you referred to this document in your report. That's why we didn't change it. But everybody will be able to compare the two. Mr. Marijan, let us now look at the direct communication between the Department of Defence with the military commanders as regards morale. Let us look at document P 1198. This is a report from the Ante Starcevic Brigade from Gornji Vakuf dated 18 January 1993, sent directly to the Defence Department and it's IDP Sector. That sector is actually the Morale Sector, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, have you seen this document or similar documents showing direct communication between military commanders and the IPD Sector?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially from this brigade and this period there are a number of similar documents where the assistant for IPD skips his direct superior and turns directly to the sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to document 4D 1156. It's the following document. It's dated 19 April 1993. The assistant commander for IPD in the Rama Brigade is sending a report directly to the Department of Defence and its IPD Sector. Does this document confirm that direct communication?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: A document that is outside the time-period of your report, but do look at it anyway, 4D 1554. The assistant minister of defence, it's called the political administration in January 1994, directly communicates with assistant commanders for political business. So can we say that the Assistant minister of defence directly communicated with the brigades on the ground?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although it is not completely clear, but as it says to the "Assistant commanders for political business." We can suppose that it was sent to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that issues that have to do with morale are within the remit of the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's why there is a sector for morale there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge or memory, did the Main Staff and its establishment have a service that would deal with morale?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, honestly, I knew a person who called himself assistant, but I have never seen that position in the establishment -- or, rather, I looked at it a short while ago, the establishment from 1992. It isn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we wanted to find out to who the brigade commander is accountable to as regards morale, and if we were to apply paragraph 9 of the Decision on the Basic Principles of Organisation of the Department of Defence, would it be right to say that the brigade commander is accountable to Bruno Stojic?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be interpreted that way, but if you let me, I would like to add something.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, as I have very little time, do make a note of your additional comment, and if I should have enough time I will deal with it at the end.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is very important.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But then Ms. Nozica can ask you that question in redirect.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not opposed to the witness saying something, but it shouldn't count against my time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Then we will deal with it in the redirect, but this witness has said that this is very important. It is obvious he wants to clarify something additionally.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wanted to say that the decision dated 15 September and 15 days earlier the zones of operation had been established. I don't know why they are not contain in the decision because the decision was made on August the 31st, if I remember well. According to me it would be right if the assistant brigade commanders through the assistant commanders for morale were accountable to Mr. Stojic as the head in the operative zone, but whoever is in the establishment of the brigade is also accountable to their commander because you could -- one could conclude that the brigade commander is not in a position to issue orders to assistants -- to his assistants for morale or something, although he could. I was in that position for a while and received orders from the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: As this part did not count against my time, I would like to make clear to the witness that now we're not talking about the communication between the brigade commander and his assistants, but, rather, that we are establishing to who the brigade commander is accountable with regard to certain issues. It is clear that the brigade commander could issue orders through his assistant for morale, but the question is to who the brigade commander was accountable for such orders. So we're now interested in the chain of command above brigade level in accordance with our paragraph 9 of the decision on the internal organisation of the Defence Department. Let us now take a look at the Security and Information Service, SIS. As General Praljak has already asked you questions about it, we'll be very fast. Please look at diagram 4D 1281. Let us show it to the witness so that he can comment on it. It is -- the diagram is a somewhat altered diagram that you have already seen, but it also now includes the armed forces. The part in blue has been added when we compare it to the one that you used. Please say if this is an accurate depiction.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the best so far.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So I conclude that you have no other -- no objections?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in accordance with the decision on the basic principles of the internal organisation, probably you singled out the military police -- military police on purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes. In answering the question -- questions of Mr. Karnavas and General Praljak, you said that the SIS was within the remit of the head of the Department of Defence, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The Security Sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You also commented some provisions of the rules governing the work of the SIS. I have also included document P 4211. Please take a look at it. I would like -- I'll focus on something you mentioned in your report, namely in paragraph 9, definition of the Department of Defence in the wider sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Nozica [as interpreted], you have asked for the admission of this document? This document, the one dated the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did not say anything about the adoption of these documents. I would just like to have us look at it. I know that this already is an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So Article 9 of this document, here you have a definition of the Defence Department in a broader sense, and you also included this into your report. Pursuant to this decision, the Defence Department consists of all sectors or sectors of the departments, the Main Staff military districts, units, assembly points, training centres, companies for the production of military equipment and so on. Is there anything you would like to comment on regarding this provision.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that when we are talking about the Defence Department in a broader sense here, the armed forces are also included, whereas I believe that we should say that we are talking about the Defence Department and the armed forces, otherwise it would follow that everything falls under the Defence Department because here even the Assembly points are mentioned which did not exist in the HVO so obviously this was copied from somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: This is something that you copied in your report but you did not comment?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I just mentioned that this was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm most interested in Article 63 of this document which says that the assistant commanders for the Information and Security Service should be required to perform the tasks of commanders of the units within whose structure they belong which pertain to the scope of the work of the service, and the next one says with respect to the implementation of the tasks with the scope of SIS the employees shall be responsible to the superior centre of administration. Is this what you confirmed to Mr. Karnavas, that the head of the Department of Defence, Mr. Stojic, was in charge of SIS rather than HVO government or any other body?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that what I said? The assistant head was indeed in charge of the security matters, and obviously within the HVO this was his remit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we now try to clarify the dilemma which we used to have and this will also serve us to assess the quality of your report. So the part that regards your paragraph in which you talk about the assistant chief for SIS within the Main Staff. We said that this is document 2D 002 -- 928. We have this document now in both the Croatian and the English language. I would kindly ask the usher to take several copies and provide Their Honours, the witness, and Mr. Stojic's counsels as well as the OTP with this. So once again the document is 2D 928. At the end of your -- can have your article 39, you say: "At the Main Staff of the HVO the assistant for SIS was not provided after the end of 1992. In later half of the 1993, such a position must have existed." As we can see from the footnote 102, this claim is based on the document 2D 00928. Now, if we look at this document, 2D 00928, Article 10 or item 10, we can see that a this was the proposal for Mate Knezovic to be appointed as the SIS office -- as the official for SIS at the Main Staff. Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So this is the proposal for the employment of a SIS employee to the Main Staff. Your conclusion regards the function of the assistant for SIS at the Main Staff. Can we conclude that the document 2D 928 has nothing to do with the position of the assistant for SIS at the Main Staff and that the statement or conclusion you drew in your report has no factual base?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. Mr. Knezovic was not appointed an assistant but he was, rather, assign to the position of an employee for -- of SIS.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijan, we tried to use the same methodology to draw some conclusions, so we said that the activities related to SIS were within the remit of the head of the Department of Defence, that at the Main Staff until the later part of 1993 in its formation or establishment had no service that would be dealing with SIS. Can we now by applying the item 9 of the decision on the basic principles of the internal organisation of the Defence Department conclude that the tasks related to -- that when it comes to the task related to SIS the brigade commander was responsible to the head of the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You only have two alternatives. He was either responsible to the Chief of the Main Staff or to the head of the Defence Department. So who was he responsible to?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an interesting question. Look --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If you cannot answer, Mr. Marijan, we shall proceed. If you cannot make that choice for any reason, we shall proceed.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of all of this, it would follow that the assistant commander was responsible to the head of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: My question relates to the brigade commander. So who did the brigade commander respond to in relation to the topics related to SIS?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I would dare say that the brigade commander was responsible to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please bear in mind all the time item 9 of the decision on the basic principles of the internal organisation of the Defence Department. Here it is stated that defence commander is subordinated and responsible to the head of the Department of Defence for the topics that fall under his remit.
